data.name: Rudrala
data.gender_notes: Rudrala is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Rudrala is a name derived from Rudra, who is a form of Lord Shiva, the God of Destruction in Hindu mythology. The name Rudrala carries the meaning “God of Destruction” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Rudrala usually hope their child will grow to embody god of destruction and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: One who embodies divine anger and power.
data.etymology: Rudrala belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Destruction.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rudrala total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rudrala holds deep cultural significance in Hinduism, particularly in India, Nepal, and other regions influenced by Hindu traditions. Rudra, the deity this name is derived from, is known for his destructive yet necessary role in the universe, often associated with transformation and renewal. God Rudra is also worshipped as a healer and remover of negative energies and diseases. His symbol, the trident, represents the three essential aspects of creation - creation, preservation, and destruction. The name Rudrala is a reflection of this rich cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: Rudrala is a name rooted in spiritual significance, for it refers to the divine presence of Lord Rudra, who is part of the Trimurti, the three supreme deities in Hinduism (Brahma, Vishnu, and Rudra). By honoring this name, the individual carrying it is connected to Lord Rudra's divine attributes. This name embodies the lingering energy of creation, destruction, and transformation, which encourages personal growth, resilience, and awareness of the cyclic nature of life. The name Rudrala carries a sacred meaning that inspires one to lead a spiritual life, seeking inner peace and understanding.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rudrala is a feminine form of Rudra, symbolizing the fierce, protective, and transformative energy of Shiva. It represents the divine force that destroys obstacles and negativity, paving the way for spiritual growth and inner peace.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas, Upanishads, or other scriptures.

historical_references.reference: Rudrala is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata, which is estimated to have been composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE. In the epic, Rudrala is described as the wife of the god Rudra, also known as Shiva.

The name Rudrala also appears in the Puranic literature, specifically in the Shiva Purana, which is believed to have been written between the 6th and 8th centuries CE. In this text, Rudrala is depicted as a form of the goddess Parvati, consort of Shiva, and the mother of the god Kartikeya.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern times, the ancient Hindu name 'Rudrala' has gained popularity beyond its traditional context as a name of a goddess in Hindu mythology. On Instagram, Rudrala is often used as a hashtag (#Rudrala) in posts related to goddess worship, particularly of the goddess Rudrani or Rudrakshi, who is believed to bring prosperity and protection. On YouTube, there are several channels dedicated to Rudrala meditation and yoga practices, which offer spiritual guidance and mental health benefits. Blogs, on the other hand, explore the symbolic meanings and historical significance of Rudrala in Hinduism, as well as its modern usage as a name or mantra in personal growth and wellness journeys.
